description.value: The study examined whether intravenous ghrelin modulates neural responses to visual food cues in healthy men, and whether these effects relate to hunger and food-picture recognition.

design.value: Twenty healthy normal-weight male subjects underwent a single fMRI session approximately 3 hr after a standardized breakfast. Twelve subjects viewed food and scenery pictures before and after ghrelin administration, while eight subjects underwent two identical control blocks without ghrelin to assess order effects.

task_description.value: During each functional run, 15 images, consisting of 7–8 food and 7–8 scenery images, were presented in random order. Each picture was shown for 5 s followed by a 15 s dark screen with a central fixation cross. Subjects were instructed to focus their attention on the stimuli.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (version 9.60, Neurobehavioral Systems, CA, USA)

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to focus their attention on the stimuli.

stimuli.value: Food and scenery pictures, previously matched for visual appeal.

recognition of food images viewed in the scanner
hedonic ratings of the images on a scale of 1 to 9

instrument.value: 1.5T Siemens Vision MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature radiofrequency head coil

description.value: T2* weighted images with BOLD contrast were acquired after a high-resolution T1-weighted anatomical scan. Thirty-two 4 mm thick slices covered the whole brain. The functional session consisted of six runs of 5 min, each consisting of 100 volumes per run. Two dummy images were taken at the onset of each sequence and discarded.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2* weighted images with BOLD contrast

description.value: Functional images were spatially smoothed with a 6 mm Gaussian filter and motion corrected prior to statistical analyses.

steps.value: Two dummy images were taken at the onset of each sequence and discarded to reduce non-steady state effects.
Spatially smoothed with a 6 mm Gaussian filter
Parametric images were transformed into Montreal Neurological Institute space

model_settings.value: Separate regressors for food and scenery pictures, consisting of boxcar functions convolved with a standard hemodynamic response function. Regional brain activation was determined by calculating a contrast of food minus scenery and computing effect and standard deviation at each brain voxel for each individual. Group analysis used a mixed effects statistical model.

estimator.value: t statistic from the effect size and standard deviation of the general linear model for each individual

interpretations.value: The t value at each voxel is a measure of the likelihood that there was greater BOLD signal in response to the food than the scenery pictures at that location in the brain.

interpretations.value: Ghrelin increased the response to food pictures in regions of the brain, including the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula, and striatum.
